text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing flaky 429 behavior from hosted API in a throughput test. Some requests get `Retry-After: 0.5` (float seconds) and some come with `x-rate-limit-reset: 1710000000` (epoch). Our client assumes int seconds for Retry-After and chokes on the float.
kevin: ahh that explains the crash I saw in the integration tests. stack trace shows int() cast failing.
samir: we've been normalizing headers in the Go client; Python one is still very thin.
maria: repro steps: run this loop with short sleeps and burst 100 reqs/s. sample response headers pasted: `{'retry-after': '0.5', 'x-rate-limit-reset': '1710000000', 'x-rate-limit-remaining': '0'}`
olga: hmm, two issues: 1) parsing floats in Retry-After, 2) handling mixed-reset headers (epoch vs relative seconds). also some older gateways return `Retry-After: 1,463` (comma thousands) which Python int() also rejects.
kevin: ugh commas. I can add a small helper to sanitize numeric headers: strip commas, allow floats, fallback to ceil(float) when scheduling backoff.
ci-bot: build #4532 failed on linux-py3.11 (test: test_rate_limit_headers) :broken_heart:
maria: test failing on CI is the same int() crash. I pushed a tiny repro to /internal/devex/playgrounds/rate-headers.py.
samir: API has two different semantics: `Retry-After` sometimes means seconds-relative, sometimes an HTTP-date. We should prefer `Retry-After` if it's parsable; otherwise use `x-rate-limit-reset` epoch. Fallback order: Retry-After -> x-rate-limit-reset -> x-rate-limit-window (if available) -> default backoff.
olga: +1. For Python SDK, propose adding `redwood.client.throttle.parse_retry_after(headers)` utility that returns an int backoff seconds, and a small async helper `await throttle.wait_for_retry(headers, loop)` that works with both sync/async clients.
kevin: will implement parse logic as: try parse RFC 1123 date, else try float/int (strip commas), else try epoch header names. Always return an int number of seconds (ceil). Also include tests for bizarre formats like `0.5`, `1,463`, `Tue, 21 Mar 2023 02:07:55 GMT`.
maria: would be sweet if the helper also returned a token-consumption hint when `x-rate-limit-remaining` present so callers can reduce concurrency proactively. e.g., return {delay: 1, remaining: 0, reset_at: 1710000000}.
olga: we should avoid nested dicts in public surface — keep simple tuple or small dataclass. But dataclass leaks typing across versions. Maybe return a namedtuple-like tuple `(delay_seconds, remaining_str)` where remaining_str is string or None.
samir: typing note: the SDK typings must mark `parse_retry_after(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> int` and an alternate `parse_retry_metadata(headers) -> Tuple[int, Optional[int], Optional[int]]`. Keep overloads minimal.
kevin: PR incoming later today. I'll include async sleep helper using `asyncio.sleep(delay)` and a sync helper using `time.sleep`.
maria: one more edgecase — for Dedicated/private customers we sometimes get `x-quota-reset-window-ms`. That's milliseconds and not documented widely. Add a normalization table in code: known headers -> unit multiplier.
olga: please add small doc snippet in the DX guide and a short example in quickstart showing how to use the throttle util with streaming calls. People trip on 429s during onboarding.
kevin: noted. I'll add changelog entry and a tiny example: ```python
from redwood.client import Client
from redwood.client.throttle import parse_retry_after, wait_for_retry
c = Client()
resp = c.generate(...)
if resp.status_code == 429:
    delay = parse_retry_after(resp.headers)
    await wait_for_retry(delay)
```
maria: thanks — also flagging product: some customers expect `Retry-After` granularity <1s for realtime apps. We should document that ceil() will be used for scheduling but allow callers to opt into fractional waits if they want (i.e., return float).
olga: agreed, make the public parse return float and an aux helper `ceil_delay()` for backcompat. Keep type hints: `-> float`.
ci-bot: test run #4533: added tests for float, comma, HTTP-date, epoch formats. all green on linux-py3.11. :rocket:
maria: awesome. can someone add a short issue for adding the sample to quickstart? I'll assign to kevin.
kevin: created issue #789 (devex) and added PR link in thread. merging after a quick review. :thumbsup:
samir: once merged, we should cut a patch release and announce in #devex and #eng. This helps customers and prevents more noisy CI failures.
olga: also update CHANGELOG and add a note to the SDK migration guide.
maria: thanks all — relieved this was a small fix. let's follow up if we see more weird header formats.
